purpose: Define qc target as an explicit canonical analysis/edit subject so qc can operate on a file, module, canonical identity, code surface or other declared target without inferring scope from conversation or filesystem proximity.

topics.name: QC Target
topics.purpose: Define qc target as an explicit canonical analysis/edit subject so qc can operate on a file, module, canonical identity, code surface or other declared target without inferring scope from conversation or filesystem proximity.

semantics.target_rule: qc target is explicit and machine-resolvable.
semantics.identity_rule: Canonical target identity remains separate from physical file path.
semantics.scope_rule: qc may only inspect/modify within its explicit target scope and invoked operation permissions.
semantics.reference_rule: Where a canonical identity exists, qc target should retain that identity even if a source file path is also present.
semantics.projection_rule: Editor/file UI selection may propose a qc target, but target semantics are explicit in the invocation/context.
semantics.authority_rule: Selecting a target does not grant write authority.

invariants.rule: q-family roles, backend aliases, targets, command namespaces and help metadata remain explicit and do not derive authority from model/backend output.

hard_gates.condition: qc target inferred solely from current directory or conversation proximity
file path substitutes for existing canonical identity
qc writes outside declared target scope
external target used without explicit external-reference semantics

references.purpose: qc writes still use authoritative change boundaries.
